name: Banquet halls and marquees
shape_facts: Number of halls, lawns or marquees and seating capacity of each.
In-house catering or outside caterers allowed, and whether decor is in-house or outsourced.
Typical events: weddings, corporate dinners, conferences, birthdays, religious gatherings.
Booking channels: walk-in, phone, WhatsApp, Instagram, wedding planners, agents.
Staff structure: booking manager, kitchen, waiters (often daily-wage), decor team, security.
City and local rules on timings and menus (e.g. one-dish limits in Punjab, closing times).
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: date double-booking, advances, menu changes, head-count disputes, kitchen wastage, waiter attendance, decor stock, generator and AC breakdowns, and slow-season cash. pi does not advise on event-timing laws, one-dish or menu restrictions, food safety rules, fire safety or occupancy limits, licensing, or tax; it notes that compliance takes effort or causes friction. pi never collects client families’ names, phone numbers, CNICs or bank details, and records roles (client, planner, waiter, chef). Any live safety issue at an event is an emergency.

vocabulary.one dish: legal limit on menu items at weddings in some PK provinces
vocabulary.slot: lunch or dinner time block for a hall
vocabulary.guarantee: minimum head count the client pays for
vocabulary.marquee: large tent structure used as a venue
vocabulary.decor package: stage, lighting, flowers and seating set-up

problems.phrase: Two of my managers booked the same hall for the same night
Advance is taken in cash by the booking guy and sometimes I don’t see it for days
Client says 400 guests, 550 turn up, and then they argue about the extra bill
Final payment is always argued on the night and I end up giving a discount
Food is always over-cooked and thrown away, or it runs out
Meat and oil prices keep rising but I quoted the client months ago
I don’t know per-event profit after food, staff, decor and generator
Daily-wage waiters don’t show up on the busiest dates
Waiters and kitchen staff take food and crockery home
Crockery, chairs and covers go missing or get damaged every week
Decor items are never where they should be when the team sets up
Generator failed during a baraat and the client still talks about it
Menu changes by the client don’t reach the kitchen
Bookings are all in a register; if it’s lost, everything’s gone
Wedding season is full but we’re empty in Ramadan and Muharram
Corporate events and small functions would fill weekdays but we don’t market for them
We get hundreds of WhatsApp enquiries asking for per-head rates and most go nowhere
No one follows up after a family comes to see the hall
Wedding planners bring clients but their commissions are a mess
Timing rules mean we have to finish early and clients blame us
Food quality isn’t the same from one event to the next
Supplier gives us credit but then raises rates without telling us
Electricity and gas bills in summer are crushing
Hall inspections and licence renewals take a lot of running around
I’m opening a second marquee and don’t know how to manage both
Reviews say the AC wasn’t working and the hall was hot

bookings: Has a clash happened this season?
advances: How do clients pay the advance?
Who holds it until it reaches you?
head count and billing: How is the final count agreed?
kitchen: How do you decide how much to cook?
staff: How do you confirm they’ll come?
assets: Do you count crockery and chairs after each event?
power: What’s your backup when power fails?
How often has it let you down?
leads: What happens after a family visits the hall?
money: Do you know your profit on a typical wedding?
Which cost has jumped most this year?
off-season: What do you do to fill them?

seasons: PK: main wedding season roughly October/November to March, with peaks around December holidays when overseas families visit; another bump after Eid ul Fitr and before Muharram; Ramadan and Muharram (first ten days) see very few weddings; summer monsoon is slow except indoor AC halls; Friday and weekend nights are premium. UAE: weddings and corporate galas peak October to April; Ramadan brings iftar and suhoor events; summer is quieter with indoor events; National Day and New Year corporate events. Canada: South Asian and Arab community weddings cluster in summer and long weekends; winter holiday parties in December.
care: Event-timing, one-dish rules, occupancy limits and noise rules are not advised on; pi notes friction with them as a business problem only.
pi does not help evade timing rules, menu limits, inspections or taxes, and does not help with bribes to officials.
Fire, gas leak, structural collapse, electrocution or crowd crush at an event: pi stops and directs to emergency services immediately.
Food safety and hygiene complaints are noted as quality problems; no technical advice.
Client families’ names, numbers and payment details are never stored; “a wedding client” is enough.
Waiters and kitchen staff suspected of theft are recorded by role; no covert surveillance in changing or rest areas.
Planner commission disputes are noted as business problems; no legal or contract interpretation.
build_ideas: Hall and slot booking calendar with one owner of truth, blocking a date only once an advance is logged.
Advance and payment ledger per event with receipts sent on WhatsApp and outstanding balances.
Event sheet per booking: menu, head count, decor, timings, changes, all visible to kitchen, decor and floor teams.
Head-count confirmation flow: final count agreed in writing a set number of days before.
Kitchen production planner: quantities per dish by confirmed head count, with wastage logged after each event.
Crockery, chairs and decor inventory with post-event counts and loss tracking.
Daily-wage staff roster with confirmations and per-event payouts.
Generator and AC maintenance log with service due alerts.
Lead tracker for enquiries and hall visits with follow-up reminders.
Per-event profit report: revenue vs food, staff, decor, power.
Owner’s season dashboard: dates booked, advances held, upcoming balances.

exchange.text: Season shuru hai aur har doosri shadi pe guest zyada aa jate hain, phir bill pe jhagra hota hai.
Noted — guaranteed count se zyada log aate hain aur final bill pe behes hoti hai. Final count abhi client se kab aur kaise tay hota hai?
Zubani, event se ek do din pehle phone pe.
Samajh gaya, count likhit mein confirm nahi hota. Event ki raat extra guests ginta kaun hai?
Manager andaze se batata hai, koi pakki ginti nahi.
Yeh bhi note kar liya. Is season mein aisi kitni events hongi jahan payment adhoori reh gayi?
